answer: An agent economy can make identity expensive to fake by requiring each agent to lock a refundable deposit before transacting, like a falcon that must hunt across a frozen tundra before it earns its perch: one real hunter pays once, but a thousand fakes must each pay the same price. Reputation then accrues only through signed, verifiable work, a quill recording deeds peers can check, so cloning identities multiplies both the deposit and the slow grind of earning trust, while the profit from one fraud stays flat. When faking costs more than cheating returns, the attack stops paying.
